entities.name: Fantastic Beasts and Where to Find Them
entities.label: Text
entities.summary:
Fantastic Beasts and Where to Find Them, published in 2001, is a notable work by British author J.K. Rowling that expands the lore of the Harry Potter universe through a fictional guide to magical creatures. This text is presented as a textbook, purportedly owned by the character Harry Potter, and is recognized for its detailed illustrations and annotations, contributing to the immersive world-building that has captivated millions since the release of the first Harry Potter book in 1997. The book serves as both a companion piece to the main series and a standalone work, illustrating Rowling's commitment to creating a rich, fantastical world that blends elements of folklore, mythology, and creativity.

The book itself is structured as a field guide, categorizing various magical creatures with notes that reflect Harry Potter's experiences and those of his friends, Ron Weasley and Hermione Granger. Notable creatures such as the Hippogriff and the Niffler are included, with descriptions that draw from a mix of real-world zoology and mythic traditions. This blending of the ordinary with the extraordinary not only entertains but also educates readers about the importance of conservation and understanding biodiversity, albeit within a fictional framework. The original edition featured illustrations by Rowling, further enhancing its appeal and scholarly value as a text within the fantasy genre.

Since its publication, Fantastic Beasts and Where to Find Them has authored a substantial legacy, leading to the creation of a film series set in the same universe, which began with a release in 2016. The book and subsequent adaptations have inspired a renewed interest in magical realism and fantasy literature, influencing both readers and writers alike. Rowling's work has transformed into a cultural phenomenon, impacting the literary landscape and leading to discussions about the themes of friendship, loyalty, and the ethical treatment of creatures, both magical and real.

Their legacy is studied through the lens of historical causation.", "summary": "Fantastic Beasts and Where to Find Them is a fictional companion book to the Harry Potter series, written by J. K. Rowling under the pen name Newt Scamander — first published in 2001 by Bloomsbury and Scholastic, presented as a reproduction of the textbook used by Hogwarts students in the Care of Magical Creatures class, with handwritten annotations by Harry Potter, Ron Weasley, and Hermione Granger. The book catalogues 75 magical creatures of the Harry Potter wizarding world (Acromantula, Basilisk, Bowtruckle, Centaur, Graphorn, Hippogriff, Niffler, Nundu, Phoenix, Thunderbird, and many others), describing each creature's classification, physical characteristics, habitat, and behaviour in the format of a naturalist's handbook, mimicking the style of a real-world zoological reference. The original 2001 edition was published as a Comic Relief fundraising book alongside Quidditch Through the Ages; a revised and expanded edition appeared in 2017.

The fictional author, Newton Artemis Fido 'Newt' Scamander, is a Magizoologist (a scholar of magical animals) who became the protagonist of a film franchise: the Fantastic Beasts film series produced by Warner Bros. (Fantastic Beasts and Where to Find Them, 2016; The Crimes of Grindelwald, 2018; The Secrets of Dumbledore, 2022), starring Eddie Redmayne as Newt Scamander, and written by Rowling herself. The film series is set in the 1920s–1940s and explores the wizarding world of that period — pre-dating the Harry Potter novels by several decades — with New York, Paris, and Brazil as settings, and the conflict between Newt Scamander and the dark wizard Gellert Grindelwald (the predecessor to Voldemort) as its primary narrative.
